story_issues: Headline buries three separate asks in one sentence — violates atomic decision principle; a CEO cannot action 'approve emergency payment authority, a ₹30,000 crore fiscal backstop, AND one UAE crude cargo' as a single instruction
Situation block is 68 words — exceeds the 30-word urgency target by more than double; the voter-visibility sentence is editorial, not a decision driver
Analysis item 03 uses a range ('5–10 days') — violates crisp numbers rule; pick 7 or 10, not a range
Analysis item 02 mixes two different facts in the finding: the UAE cargo detail AND the Bathinda shutdown consequence — WHAT/WHY/WHAT TO DO structure collapses into one run-on
Decision 2 bundles three separate actions under one owner-deadline pair (confirm cargo, cut capacity to 70%, issue cooking-gas order) — not atomic; each needs its own owner and deadline
Decision 3 is truncated mid-sentence ('Approve fiscal transfer by April') — content is missing entirely, breaking the decision pyramid

Context banner line 1 is a compound sentence with three unrelated facts — a non-specialist cannot parse the causal chain; Hormuz closure → $156/bbl → Russia waiver expiry needs a single crisp connective statement
KPI card 2 says 'Southern cooking-gas buffer (Karnataka / Goa)' — Goa is irrelevant noise and dilutes the southern India narrative established in the situation block; pick one geography

Pyramid structure partially correct at document level (conclusion headline first) but each analysis item inverts: items 01 and 03 put the 'so what' action last rather than leading with it, then proving it
The ₹30,000 crore figure in the headline does not appear in any KPI card or analysis item — number is unanchored and unverifiable within the document
